Lessons.Title: Multiplication of Multi-digit Numbers
ExplanationParagraphs:
Learning goal: You will deepen your understanding of the connections between algorithms that use partial products and the standard algorithm when multiplying a pair of two-digit numbers.
In an earlier unit, you analyzed and experimented with different ways to multiply multi-digit numbers by single-digit whole numbers. This included analyzing diagrams and series of equations, including those that represented algorithms that use partial products. You were introduced to the standard algorithm of multiplication and its connections to other ways of reasoning about products, particularly algorithms that use partial products.

2021 source activity sequence: Warm-up: Estimation Exploration: A Silly Riddle (10 minutes); Activity 1: Two Methods Revisited (20 minutes); Activity 2: Two by Two (15 minutes); Cool-down: Four by One and Two by Two (5 minutes)
Math focus: A two-digit by two-digit product can be represented as partial products and reconciled to the standard algorithm.
Worked Edulytics example: Decompose 14 as 10 + 4. 23 × 14 = 23 × 10 + 23 × 4 = 230 + 92. Add partial products to obtain 322; align place values in the standard algorithm.
First-party Edulytics Cool-down (publisher's original not inspected): Find 26 × 13 using partial products.
